agricultural: broad cultivated land with regular field texture and open farmland layout, distinguishing agricultural from tenniscourt by lacking small rectangular court markings, from runway by lacking a long straight paved strip, and from forest by lacking dense continuous tree canopy.
airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway which appears as a long straight paved strip without a discrete fuselage.
baseballdiamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield, distinguishing baseballdiamond from golfcourse by lacking landscaped fairways, from mobilehomepark by lacking repetitive trailer-like housing rows, and from buildings by lacking large roof-dominant built structures.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary, distinguishing beach from chaparral by lacking dry shrub-covered terrain and from river by showing a broader coastal shoreline rather than a narrow winding channel.
buildings: large roofed man-made structures with block-like geometry and organized built-up layout, distinguishing buildings from denseresidential by stronger individual roof mass, from parkinglot by having dominant building footprints rather than open paved space, and from sparseresidential by stronger structural dominance and less open spacing.
chaparral: irregular dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from river by lacking a continuous water channel and from beach by lacking a bright sand-water shoreline.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing denseresidential from mobilehomepark by less uniform trailer-row organization, from mediumresidential by much closer building intervals, and from buildings by smaller and more repetitive housing roofs.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture and little visible built structure, distinguishing forest from mediumresidential by lacking neighborhood roof patterns and from agricultural by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous road surface and branching traffic structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended horizontal road flow, from runway by lacking aviation-strip context, and from intersection by being a longer corridor rather than a compact junction node.
golfcourse: well-maintained green fairways with landscaped grass regions and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golfcourse from baseballdiamond by lacking a compact diamond infield and from mobilehomepark by lacking repetitive trailer-like housing rows.
harbor: waterfront port area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from parkinglot by the presence of water and dock-side organization and from storagetanks by stronger harbor-water context rather than isolated circular industrial containers.
intersection: road crossing region where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from freeway by emphasizing a compact junction node, from denseresidential by road-dominant geometry rather than dense housing roofs, and from overpass by lacking a strongly elevated crossing structure.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible yards and balanced housing density, distinguishing mediumresidential from denseresidential by larger spacing between houses, from forest by lacking continuous tree canopy, and from sparseresidential by showing a denser neighborhood grouping.
mobilehomepark: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobilehomepark from denseresidential by its more uniform trailer-like layout, from sparseresidential by denser and more regular placement, and from parkinglot by lacking large open vehicle rows.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form, from intersection by stronger elevated roadway overlap, and from runway by lacking a long flat aviation strip.
parkinglot: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parkinglot from buildings by lacking dominant roofed structures, from harbor by lacking water and dock infrastructure, and from mobilehomepark by lacking repetitive trailer-like housing rows.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from chaparral by clear water appearance and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open surroundings, distinguishing runway from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body, from freeway by lacking complex road branching, and from buildings by lacking dense roofed built structures.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparseresidential from buildings by weaker roof mass concentration, from mobilehomepark by lacking regular trailer-row organization, and from mediumresidential by much larger spacing between houses.
storagetanks: large circular or cylindrical industrial containers with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storagetanks from mobilehomepark by lacking trailer-like housing rows, from harbor by weaker dock-water context, and from buildings by emphasizing circular industrial tank shapes rather than block-like roofs.
tenniscourt: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated sports-court geometry, distinguishing tenniscourt from denseresidential by lacking residential roof clusters, from agricultural by lacking field parcel texture, and from mobilehomepark by lacking trailer-like housing rows.
